findings.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java:hasPermission uses findByName(server, groupId) but group resources are named with prefix 'group.resource.' + id, so lookup always returns null and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource, breaking per-group permissions (over-granting)
[High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java:canManage grants manage access when caller only has VIEW scope on all-groups via hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE); view-only should not imply manage

[High/security] UsersResource.java:searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.java removed per-user filter usersEvaluator::canView, relying solely on GROUPS session attribute; when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns empty set the search is unfiltered, potentially exposing users the caller cannot view

[Medium/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java:hasPermission invokes AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) creating the all-groups resource (a write) as a side effect of read-path evaluation, adding store writes/churn on every denied check

[Medium/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java canList() is not overridden so it only checks admin roles, contradicting javadoc that V2 grants listing via VIEW/MANAGE group permissions; admins with only group-level permissions cannot list groups
[Medium/doc_defect] GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:requireManageMembers javadoc says it throws if canManageMembership returns false, but implementation checks canViewMembers; wrong method referenced

[Medium/doc_defect] GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:canManageMembership javadoc says it returns true if UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage() is true, but implementation checks MANAGE_USERS role / group MANAGE or MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes; documented semantics don't match

[Medium/bug] GroupPermissions.java:requireViewMembers behavior changed from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers(group), and canViewMembers now also accepts MANAGE_MEMBERS, silently broadening view access to manage-only admins; verify this is intended

[Low/bug] AdminPermissionsSchema.java:resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name unlike resolveUser/resolveClient, so resources are named by UUID instead of a human-readable group path/name

[Low/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java lacks a test for the empty-groupIdsWithViewPermission case (cross-realm admin or admin with no group permissions) where the removed per-user filter could leak users
[Low/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java lacks a test asserting a VIEW-only all-groups permission does NOT grant manage operations, which would catch the canManage() over-grant

[Low/bug] BruteForceUsersResource.java:searchForUser dropped the if (!auth.users().canView()) guard, so the GROUPS session attribute is set even for callers who can view all users, unnecessarily constraining search results for fully-privileged admins

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java:hasPermission uses findByName(server, groupId) but group resources are named with prefix 'group.resource.' + id, so lookup always returns null and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource, breaking per-group permissions (over-granting)

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates resources via resourceStore.findByType(...) and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and also adds granted.add(groupResource.getId()). But hasPermission() interprets its first argument as a *group id/name* and does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Passing a Resource's internal ID into findByName will not match (name != id), so the lookup will typically return null and the method will fall back to the type-level "all-groups" resource (or return false). This breaks per-group permission evaluation and can result in incorrect grants/filters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java:canManage grants manage access when caller only has VIEW scope on all-groups via hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE); view-only should not imply manage
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly grants manage access when a caller only has VIEW scope due to the hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) fallback, which is exactly the golden issue (canManage should require MANAGE only, while canView can accept VIEW or MANAGE).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] UsersResource.java:searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.java removed per-user filter usersEvaluator::canView, relying solely on GROUPS session attribute; when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns empty set the search is unfiltered, potentially exposing users the caller cannot view

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit per-user permission filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser` (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now always calls `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` unfiltered. The only remaining restriction added here is setting the session attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` *only if* `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. When that set is empty (e.g., caller lacks global view and has no group-based view-members grants), no session restriction is applied and the user search stream is no longer filtered by `usersEvaluator`, so results could include users the caller cannot view. The same pattern is applied in `BruteForceUsersResource` (though it previously didn’t filter either), making the permission enforcement regression most evident in `UsersResource`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java:hasPermission invokes AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) creating the all-groups resource (a write) as a side effect of read-path evaluation, adding store writes/churn on every denied check

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), the code does call AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) when a per-group Resource is not found, but the diff does not show what getResourceTypeResource() does. There is no diff-evidence that this call performs a write/creates the all-groups resource, nor that it causes store churn on denied checks. The finding asserts a specific side-effect (resource creation/write) that cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.java canList() is not overridden so it only checks admin roles, contradicting javadoc that V2 grants listing via VIEW/MANAGE group permissions; admins with only group-level permissions cannot list groups

adjudication.rationale: In V2, `GroupPermissions.canList()` is inherited (not overridden) and evaluates `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`. But `GroupPermissionsV2.canView()` only checks for an “all-groups” permission via `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)` and does not consider per-group VIEW/MANAGE permissions (`canView(GroupModel)` does, but it’s not used by `canList`). Therefore, an admin with only group-level permissions (no QUERY_GROUPS role and no all-groups VIEW/MANAGE permission) would fail `canList()`, which conflicts with the updated javadoc claiming V2 listing is granted via VIEW/MANAGE group permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/doc_defect] GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:requireManageMembers javadoc says it throws if canManageMembership returns false, but implementation checks canViewMembers; wrong method referenced

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionEvaluator, the Javadoc for requireManageMembers() incorrectly references canManageMembership(GroupModel): `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false` (it should reference canManageMembers). The finding’s claim that the implementation checks canViewMembers is not verifiable from this diff (no requireManageMembers implementation change shown), but the Javadoc mismatch itself is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/doc_defect] GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:canManageMembership javadoc says it returns true if UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage() is true, but implementation checks MANAGE_USERS role / group MANAGE or MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes; documented semantics don't match

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the Javadoc for `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManageMembership(GroupModel)` does **not** say it returns true when `UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` is true. It states it returns true if the caller has `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS`, or has permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` the group or `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP` of the group. That aligns with the shown implementations (e.g., `GroupPermissionsV2#canManageMembership` checks `MANAGE_USERS` role or group `MANAGE`/`MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP` scopes). The finding misreads the Javadoc.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] GroupPermissions.java:requireViewMembers behavior changed from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers(group), and canViewMembers now also accepts MANAGE_MEMBERS, silently broadening view access to manage-only admins; verify this is intended

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `requireViewMembers` in `GroupPermissions` to call `canViewMembers(group)` instead of the removed `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`, and `canViewMembers` is updated to accept both `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE` and `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE`. However, the prior `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` *already* allowed viewing members when the caller had either `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE` **or** `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` (`hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`), so this does not “silently broaden” access relative to the old behavior of `requireViewMembers`. The change mainly consolidates logic into `canViewMembers` so other callers (e.g., `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup` now uses `root.groups()::canViewMembers`) preserve the same semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] AdminPermissionsSchema.java:resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name unlike resolveUser/resolveClient, so resources are named by UUID instead of a human-readable group path/name

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` looks up a `GroupModel` by id and then returns `group.getId()` as the resource name (UUID). That does make group resources named by UUID rather than a human-readable name/path, unlike the likely intent of `resolveUser/resolveClient` (which typically resolve to username/clientId). However, nothing in the diff shows this causes broken behavior; in fact `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` later calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, which aligns with using the group id as the resource name. So this is more a consistency/operability concern (readability of resource names), not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java lacks a test for the empty-groupIdsWithViewPermission case (cross-realm admin or admin with no group permissions) where the removed per-user filter could leak users

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit per-user visibility filter in user searches (e.g., UsersResource.searchForUser: removed `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream` into `toRepresentation`). At the same time it only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `groupIds` is non-empty, where `groupIds` comes from the new `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (which can return an empty set for cross-realm admins or admins with no group permissions; see GroupPermissions#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission and GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returning empty in those cases). GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest covers positive cases (VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS) but does not cover the empty-set case that is most sensitive given the removed filter. While the diff alone doesn’t prove a leak (it depends on what `toRepresentation` does), the missing test for this new edge case is a concrete, diff-grounded gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java lacks a test asserting a VIEW-only all-groups permission does NOT grant manage operations, which would catch the canManage() over-grant

adjudication.rationale: The new test class `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` adds coverage for VIEW and MANAGE permissions (e.g., `testViewGroups()` and `testManageAllGroups()`), but it does not include a negative test that an all-groups permission with only `VIEW` does not allow manage operations like creating/updating groups. This is especially relevant because `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` in the diff falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, so a VIEW-only all-groups permission could incorrectly satisfy `canManage()`. A targeted test would catch/guard against this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] BruteForceUsersResource.java:searchForUser dropped the if (!auth.users().canView()) guard, so the GROUPS session attribute is set even for callers who can view all users, unnecessarily constraining search results for fully-privileged admins

adjudication.rationale: Although the explicit `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard was removed in `BruteForceUsersResource#searchForUser`, the new logic calls `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when that set is non-empty. Per the diff, `GroupPermissions#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns `Collections.emptySet()` when `root.users().canView()` is true, so fully-privileged admins (who can view all users) will not have the GROUPS session attribute set and their searches will not be constrained.
